title: How far does the cyclist ride in three weeks?
description: A cyclist rides five kilometres every day in the first week, and the daily distance grows by z kilometres each week. The distance of each week is written with a bracket, opened, and the three weeks are added.
teaching_notes: One idea: the daily distance grows by z every week, and each week has seven days, so the week's distance is seven times the daily distance. Watch for students who add z only once for the third week.

video_script.why: A learner uses the method of the bracket: a number outside a bracket multiplies every term inside, and the like terms are then joined.
video_script.substitution: The method of opening a bracket such as two times the bracket y minus one, with seven times the bracket five plus z for a week of cycling.
video_script.anchor: a cyclist riding daily for three weeks, with the daily distance written for each week
video_script.payoff_line: {{NAME_4}} cycles one hundred and five plus twenty one z kilometres in three weeks

final_answer.spoken: one hundred and five plus twenty one z kilometres

never_show: the finished total before the answer beat
maths_rules: week 2: daily distance 5 + z, so (5 + z) x 7 = 35 + 7z km
week 3: daily distance 5 + 2z, so (5 + 2z) x 7 = 35 + 14z km
video_script.design: One idea: the daily distance grows by z each week, a week has seven days, and the three weeks are added. Assumes the example of opening a bracket. A table of three weeks stays on the stage.

narration: <bookmark mark='p1'/>This question is from your book.
<bookmark mark='p2'/>{{NAME_4}} is preparing for a cycling race and practises daily.
<bookmark mark='p3'/>In the first week, {{NAME_4}} cycles five kilometres every day. Every week, the daily distance goes up by z kilometres.
<bookmark mark='p4'/>How many kilometres has {{NAME_4}} cycled after three weeks?

beats.on_screen: the cyclist and the three weeks stay on the board; Keeko sits at the corner of the board

marks.think: Keeko sits at the corner of the board

narration: <bookmark mark='think'/>Think and tell.

beats.on_screen: a week has 7 days ; distance in a week = daily distance × 7

marks.g1: a week of seven days is drawn
marks.g2: daily distance times seven is written under the week

narration: <bookmark mark='g1'/>A week has seven days.
<bookmark mark='g2'/>The distance in a week is the daily distance times seven.

beats.on_screen: Given: 5 km every day in week 1 ; the daily distance grows by z km each week

marks.gv1: 5 km a day is written for week 1
marks.gv2: z km more each week is written

narration: <bookmark mark='gv1'/>Given, {{NAME_4}} cycles five kilometres every day in the first week.
<bookmark mark='gv2'/>The daily distance grows by z kilometres each week.

beats.on_screen: To find: the total distance in 3 weeks
narration: <bookmark mark='fd'/>We find the total distance in three weeks. We work the same way as the example in your book, opening the brackets.
<bookmark mark='s1a'/>First, week one. Five kilometres a day for seven days is five times seven, which is thirty five kilometres.

beats.on_screen: Step 2: week 2: daily distance 5 + z, so (5 + z) × 7 = 35 + 7z km

marks.s2a: 5 + z is written as the daily distance

narration: <bookmark mark='s2a'/>Second, week two. The daily distance is five plus z. The week's distance is the bracket five plus z times seven.
<bookmark mark='s2b'/>Seven multiplies both terms in the bracket. That gives thirty five plus seven z kilometres.

beats.on_screen: Step 3: week 3: daily distance 5 + 2z, so (5 + 2z) × 7 = 35 + 14z km

marks.s3a: 5 + 2z is written as the daily distance

narration: <bookmark mark='s3a'/>Third, week three. The daily distance has grown by z twice, so it is five plus two z.
<bookmark mark='s3b'/>Seven times the bracket five plus two z is thirty five plus fourteen z kilometres.
<bookmark mark='s4a'/>Fourth, add the three weeks. The plain numbers are thirty five three times, which is one hundred and five.
<bookmark mark='s4b'/>The z terms are seven z and fourteen z, which make twenty one z.

beats.on_screen: Step 5, check with z = 1: daily 5, 6, 7 gives 35 + 42 + 49 = 126, and 105 + 21 = 126

marks.s5c: the weeks 35, 42 and 49 are added to 126

narration: <bookmark mark='s5a'/>Fifth, check with z as one. The daily distances are five, six and seven.
<bookmark mark='s5c'/>The weeks give thirty five, forty two and forty nine. Their sum is one hundred and twenty six.
<bookmark mark='s5b'/>The expression gives one hundred and five plus twenty one, which is also one hundred and twenty six.
<bookmark mark='ans'/>{{NAME_4}} cycles one hundred and five plus twenty one z kilometres in three weeks.
